messages:
Aisha (Product): Heads-up — during the console QA pass I noticed a bunch of in-product docs links that point to high-level pages instead of the exact panel sections. Feels janky for users trying to find a specific setting.

Ravi (Design): Yep saw that too. The help flyout links to /docs/console but the sidecar intends to jump to a subsection. On mobile the jump lands mid-header so it looks broken.

Leah (Docs): We currently generate anchors from headings like `## Prompt templates` which are fragile when copy changes. That explains some of the 404-ish landings.

Tom - DevEx: Could we use stable, explicit anchor IDs in the docs source? e.g. `### Prompt templates {#prompt-templates}` so the console always links to `.../docs/console#prompt-templates`.

Aisha (Product): That would be great. Also want to discuss terminology: console uses "Help" in the topbar but the docs site calls it "Documentation" and internal lexicon prefers "Console docs". Users get confused which one to click.

Leah (Docs): Agree — we should canonicalize to one string. Proposal: label the in-app panel "Docs" and show the full page title "Redwood Console docs" in the site. I'll open a tiny lexicon PR.

Ravi (Design): UX practicals: when we deep-link into a subheading, we should offset the scroll so the heading isn't hidden under the fixed topbar. Also add a smooth scroll behavior so it doesn't feel like a jump.

Tom - DevEx: Accessibility nit: ensure `#` anchors have descriptive link text for screen readers. Also add `aria-describedby` where needed. Current behaviour: link goes to anchor but screen reader misses context.

Leah (Docs): I'll add stable IDs and update anchors. Two questions: 1) preferred anchor naming scheme? kebab-case vs id tokens? 2) do we want versioned anchors (v1, v2) for major rewrites?

Aisha (Product): 1) Keep kebab-case, consistent with our docs pipeline. 2) For versioning let's rely on the docs site versioning mechanism rather than encode versions into anchors. If we ever move content, we should add a redirect map.

Ravi (Design): UX pattern for in-product crosslinks: 1) deep-link icons (open in docs) next to headings in the sidecar, 2) hover tooltip showing short blurb from the docs page, 3) a small breadcrumb back to the console.

Tom - DevEx: Implementation note: the sidecar should call the docs API to fetch a short summary for that anchor (cache TTL 24h) to avoid shipping full markdown. Fallback if anchor missing: open top-level docs and show a small toast "Section moved — opening docs home" with a :information_source: icon.

Leah (Docs): I'll add suggested copy for the hover tooltip and the toast: "Open documentation for this setting (opens in new tab)" and "This section moved — opening the Console docs home. Use the search to find the updated section."

Aisha (Product): Sounds good. Last thing: we need a small regression test in our QA checklist that verifies 3 random deep links from the console correctly land on the intended anchor (including mobile). Can someone own that?

ConsoleHelpBot: Reminder: action items created: update-lexicon-PR (Leah), docs-stable-anchors (Leah + Tom), UI-offset-scroll (Ravi), QA-deep-link-checklist (Aisha).

Ravi (Design): I can prototype offset scroll + popover microcopy by EOD.

Leah (Docs): I'll open the anchor PR and add redirect rules for any renamed headings. Targeting end of week.

Tom - DevEx: I'll add the API endpoint for anchor summaries and the toast behavior. Happy to pair with Ravi on the scroll behavior.

Aisha (Product): Awesome — thanks team. One follow-up: let's agree on the canonical link format in the PR description so integrators (support/Sales) can use it in KBs. Example format I like: `https://docs.redwood.inference/console/<page>#<kebab-anchor>`.

Ravi (Design): :thumbsup:

Leah (Docs): noted — will include examples.

Aisha (Product): Closing the loop — ping me once the QA checklist item exists and we'll ship a small console patch with the updated copy and the stable links.

Tom - DevEx: Will do.
